title: Conversation session snapshotting and hotspoting playbook
author: Mariana Ortiz
body:
Summary

This playbook describes a standard for capturing, storing, and operating on conversation session snapshots to support long-context evaluation, probe hotspot detection, quantization-aware replay, and accelerated regression triage. It is intended for ML engineers, SREs operating eval fleets, and product teams running shadow/shard validation.

Why we snapshot sessions

- Preserve end-to-end conversational context for repro and targeted probes.
- Enable efficient replay to shadow fleets and quantized variants without exposing PII.
- Surface hotspots (slices with repeated failures: hallucination, format regressions, latency spikes).
- Reduce triage time by providing a compact, deterministic artifact for investigation.

Scope and applicability

- Applies to: streaming chat, multi-turn assistant flows, and multi-tool functioncall sessions.
- Not for: single-turn low-context stateless APIs (use existing probe farms instead).

Snapshot schema (recommended canonical fields)

- session_id: stable identifier (UUID v4)
- tenant_id: tenant or product unit (hashed for privacy)
- timestamp_first_turn: ISO-8601
- timestamp_last_turn: ISO-8601
- turn_count: integer
- turns: list of turn metadata (role, token_count, truncated boolean, priming_id)
- kv_cache_seed: small deterministic fingerprint of key-cache contents (not raw KV)
- routing_variant: model shard/variant used (e.g., gptx-9b-quant-v2)
- quality_signals: map of probe-level signals (coherence_score, err_count, latency_ms_p50/p95)
- redaction_markers: list of indices/redaction hashes applied

Example snapshot (JSON preview)

{
  "session_id": "f3a1c9b2-...",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-8a3 (hashed)",
  "timestamp_first_turn": "2026-02-10T15:21:04Z",
  "turn_count": "6",
  "routing_variant": "redwood-gpt-14b-quant2",
  "quality_signals": "coherence:0.71;latency_p95_ms:420"
}

(Implementation note: snapshots are allowed to be coarse-grained strings for fields above to avoid nested objects in storage layer.)

Retention, privacy and redaction rules

1) Retention windows
   - Default: 30 days for production shadow snapshots, 90 days for regression escrow snapshots created by oncall.
   - Long-term archival (1+ years) allowed only with executive approval and explicit legal tagging.

2) PII redaction pipeline (mandatory)
   - Run automated PII detectors (email, ssn, phone, credit-card) and replace matches with stable redaction markers.
   - Keep a hash of removed segments to allow deterministic matching without reconstituting sensitive content.

Snapshot capture workflow (operational steps)

1) Triggering captures
   - Passive capture: sample 1:10,000 sessions from production for heatmap generation.
   - Hot-capture: when sentinel probes or automated quality monitors cross thresholds (coherence delta >0.15, hallucination ratio >0.08), create hotspot snapshots immediately.
   - Manual capture: oncall or model team can request a snapshot via the ops CLI `ri snapshot create --session <id>`

2) Capture pipeline steps
   1. Fetch session record and metadata from runtime trace store.
   2. Run redaction pipeline and compute hashes.
   3. Compute KV-cache fingerprint and routing_variant.
   4. Attach telemetry (latency p50/p95, token counts, model logits summary) and commit to snapshot store.

3) Labels and metadata applied at capture time
   - `snapshot.type`: passive|hotspot|manual
   - `snapshot.privacy_level`: low|medium|high (affects who can retrieve)
   - `snapshot.fidelity`: full|minimal (whether internals/logits included)

Hotspot detection and scoring

- Hotspot score = weighted sum: w1*coherence_delta + w2*hallucination_rate + w3*latency_p95_norm + w4*turn_dispersion. Default weights: w1=0.4, w2=0.3, w3=0.2, w4=0.1.
- Thresholds: score > 0.6 -> triage ticket auto-opened; 0.4–0.6 -> queue for investigator review.

Probe synthesis from snapshots (for eval harness)

- Use snapshot turn anchors to synthesize probes that maintain token budget and priming distribution.
- When producing quantization-aware probes: annotate probes with `kv_cache_seed` and `routing_variant` so quantized runtime can reproduce cache-effect behavior.
- Probe naming convention: `snap-<session_id>-turn-<n>-quantaware`

Quantization and replay guidance

- Avoid replaying raw logits into quantized runtimes. Instead:
  - Recompute response under the target quant variant using the captured prompt and hashed-kv fingerprint.
  - Compare response embeddings + coherence metric to the baseline.
- Maintain a per-variant calibration table with expected coherence drift tolerances (example below).

Calibration table (example)

| Variant | avg_coherence_drift_allowed | latency_p95_budget_ms | note |
|---------|-----------------------------:|----------------------:|------|
| quant-v1 | 0.06 | 350 | early-stage quant |
| quant-v2 | 0.10 | 420 | aggressive memory savings |

Regression triage playbook (fast path)

1) Auto-detect: hotspot triggers and snapshot creation.
2) Triage lead inspects snapshot summary dashboard (fidelity, redaction, signals).
3) Re-run synthesized probes across shadow variants (baseline, quantized, cached/un-cached).
4) If regression reproduces: escalate to model-oncall and create a rollback/carveout plan.
5) If non-reproducible: mark as stochastic; schedule longer-term probe amplification and additional telemetry capture.

Operational runbook snippets

- CLI: create manual snapshot\  ri snapshot create --session f3a1c9b2 --fidelity full --reason "support ticket #3421"
- Fetch snapshot summary\  ri snapshot describe --id f3a1c9b2
- Re-run probe on quant variant (example)\  ri replay run --snapshot f3a1c9b2 --variant redwood-gpt-14b-quant2 --compare baseline

Ownership and SLAs

- Snapshot capture service: owning team = eval-infrastructure (SRE).
- Snapshot store availability SLA: 99.9% monthly (operational target).
- Oncall rotation: eval-oncall (primary) for triage within 4 business hours for auto-opened hotspot tickets.

Monitoring and metrics to expose

- Snapshot creation rate (per hour), hot-capture fraction, avg redact-failures, triage lead response time, probe-reproduction-rate.

Appendix A: privacy checklist (must be OK before any snapshot is exported to external vendor)

- PII scan run and zero matches (or matches replaced with redaction markers).
- Tenant opt-out respected.
- Legal export approval present in snapshot metadata.

Appendix B: common failure patterns and quick remediations

- Pattern: quantized variant shows higher brevity and missing list items.
  Quick fix: tighten temperature + enable dequantization fallback for enumerations.
- Pattern: tail-latency spikes on specific routing_variant.
  Quick fix: shift traffic to compatible shard and open capacity allocation ticket.
